Question
========



Gesucht ist die Syntax, die folgendes Diagramm erstellt:

```{r eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE}
de <- map_data("world", region = "Germany")

# ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
#   geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black")

ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  coord_quickmap()
```


**A**

```
de <- map_data("world", region = "Germany")

ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black")
```

**B**

```
de <- map_data("world")

ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black")

```


**C**

```
de <- map_data("world")

ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  coord_quickmap()
```



**D**

```
de <- map_data("world", region = "Germany")

ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  coord_quickmap()
```


**E**

```
de <- map_data("world", region = "France")

ggplot(de, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  coord_quickmap()
```





Answerlist
----------
* Antwort A
* Antwort B
* Antwort C
* Antwort D
* Antwort E



Solution
========

Antwort D; s. [hier](https://www.datanovia.com/en/blog/how-to-create-a-map-using-ggplot2/) eine Vertiefung
